text:
maya: Pasting the new dashboard mock — need a quick design/eng pass on legend density, unit abbreviations, smoothing state copy, and how we surface outliers to screen readers. Mock: https://files.redwood.ai/ux/new-dashboard-compact.png

devin: First pass: legend looks cluttered when there are 6+ series. Can we collapse less-used series into a "More" group with an inline count? Eg: "Services (4 more)" -> expand. Keeps height stable.

katie: Agree. Also propose a compact legend layout where color swatches are 8px squares with 10px spacing. That improves scan on dense charts. But keep an option to show full labels in a popover.

omar: Accessibility note: color-only labels are problematic. Ensure each legend item has a visible label text and an accessible name. Suggest adding aria-keyshortcuts for keyboard toggle: eg "Enter toggles series". Also for colorblind mode, switch to patterned strokes in the canvas renderer.

lee: Units: prefer dynamic SI formatting but show original unit in axis aria-label. Example aria: "Latency (ms) - axis showing milliseconds". For large values show suffixes (k, M) but the tooltip should show exact numbers with separators.

zara: Smoothing copy: instead of binary "Smoothed"/"Raw", use "Smoothing: Off / 7-sample" like a state label. For discoverability, clicking the label should open the smoothing menu; avoid hidden gear menus.

maya: UX question: should smoothing be applied client-side for previews, or server-side? We preferred server for consistent results across pages. Thoughts?

devin: Server-side gives consistent evals and makes caching easier. Client-side is cheaper but inconsistent. Recommendation: server smoothing for persisted charts, client smoothing for quick hover previews.

katie: On outliers: visualize two tiers — "flagged" (high confidence) and "suspicious" (low confidence). Use higher-contrast marker for flagged. For small markers ensure 4.5:1 contrast or add 2px ring.

omar: For screen readers, include a concise chart summary button that reads: "Chart summary: last 24h average 3,200 rps. 2 flagged outliers at 02:14 and 13:11. Press to open details." Use aria-live when new outliers are detected.

lee: Keyboard nav: legend must be tabbable; each item gets role="button" and aria-pressed state. When toggling series visibility, announce "Series X hidden" via sr-only live region.

zara: Microcopy tweak: change the export tooltip from "Download CSV" to "Export raw samples (CSV)" — clarifies that smoothing is not applied to exports unless explicitly requested.

maya: Design trade-off: if we add "patterned strokes" for colorblind mode, chart noise increases. Maybe enable it only when a user toggles accessibility preferences.

devin: Implementation note: patterned strokes on canvas are heavier CPU-wise but acceptable for charts with <= 10 series. For >10 we should fallback to high-contrast color palette + bold strokes.

katie: Small UI detail: when the legend collapses into a "More" group, animate height smoothly to avoid layout jank. Also prefer transform-based animations.

omar: Outlier announcement example for aria: "Outlier detected at 2026-03-22 02:14: 14,200 requests; 2.3% above 24h baseline." Make sure timezone respects user prefs.

maya: Action items summary: 1) Collapse overflow series into a "More (N)" group with accessible expand; 2) Compact swatches + popover for full labels; 3) Smoothing state label (click to open) and server-side smoothing for persisted views; 4) Two-tier outlier markers + >=4.5:1 contrast; aria-live announcements for new outliers; 5) Keyboard/ARIA behaviors for legend items and series toggles; 6) Export copy clarified.
